messages.author: 3126d00d0b94540e
messages.subject: Installation issue
parts:
I'm not sure this is a TMB issue, but it is sure stopping me from installing TMB.

I recently updated my OS to linux mint cinnamon.
$ uname -a
Linux kihikihi 5.3.0-46-generic #38~18.04.1-Ubuntu SMP Tue Mar 31 04:17:56 UTC 2020 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linu

New compiler
$ gcc --version
gcc (GCC) 10.0.1 20200212 (experimental)

Newish R
R version 3.4.4 (2018-03-15)

When I try to install TMB with install.packages('TMB'), it fails with the following message:
** building package indices
Error : requireNamespace("Matrix", quietly = TRUE) is not TRUE
ERROR: installing package indices failed
* removing ‘/usr/local/lib/R/site-library/Matrix’
ERROR: dependencies ‘Matrix’, ‘Rcpp’ are not available for package ‘RcppEigen’
* removing ‘/usr/local/lib/R/site-library/RcppEigen’
ERROR: dependencies ‘Matrix’, ‘RcppEigen’ are not available for package ‘TMB’
* removing ‘/usr/local/lib/R/site-library/TMB’

The downloaded source packages are in
    ‘/tmp/RtmpSf45vn/downloaded_packages’
Warning messages:
1: In install.packages("TMB") :
  installation of package ‘Rcpp’ had non-zero exit status
2: In install.packages("TMB") :
  installation of package ‘Matrix’ had non-zero exit status
3: In install.packages("TMB") :
  installation of package ‘RcppEigen’ had non-zero exit status
4: In install.packages("TMB") :
  installation of package ‘TMB’ had non-zero exit status
> library(TMB)

Searching the innertube reveals that there may be unaddressed issues with installing the Matrix package. I've tried several different approaches but I'm not getting any satisfaction.

Does anyone have any experience with this issue? Or a workaround?

Thanks.

messages.author: 5f950c9713997d19
messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Installation issue
parts:
Hi John

This winter, I switched over to first Linux Mint and then LMDE4 from Win10 (now using the latter). I spent a fair bit of time figuring out the R and TMB installation process for these OSs. I installed R from source, ensuring that all the dependencies were met. For the Ubuntu installation (Linus Mint), here are the steps that I followed (similar for LMDE4 except for the repository):

  1. Add following line to end of .bashrc file in the home directory

            export PATH=~/:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/local/games:/usr/games:/usr/local/ sbin:/usr/sbin:/sbin   # need to make sure that the binaries can be found

  1. Download Source tarfile (https://cran.r-project.org/) and put into R-3.6.3 (version I installed) subdirectory under home directory (~) and extract all files. Installation of many files will ultimately be in this directory; Instructions in README and INSTALL files

  2. Check that following tools are installed (LM Software Manager)

    • G++
    • Build-Essential
    • G Fortran
    • Default-Jdk

  3. In Software Sources utility, add repositories

    • Turn on Source Code repository toggle
    • To Additional Repositories, add
      • deb https://cloud.r-project.org/bin/linux/ubuntu bionic-cran35/
  4. In Software Sources utility, enter fingerprint to public key in Download tab
    1. E298A3A825C0D65DFD57CBB651716619E084DAB9
  5. sudo apt update                                                                                                    # make sure that all packages are up to date; might need to execute sudo apt upgrade
  6. sudo apt build-dep r-base > output_builddeprbase                                               # installs all dependencies for r-base (requires URI in Sources.list.d directory) & if desired stores output in output_builddeprbase
  7. ./configure –enable-R-shlib &> output_configure to create a Makefile    # will install binaries in usr/local/bin
  8. make &> output_make
  9. make check &> output_makecheck                                                                       # does some checks of the installation; not essential but good to do
  10. sudo make install &> output_makeinstall                                                              # installs software; by default, binaries are installed in the usr/local/bin/<program name> directory unless ./configure option specifies otherwise
  11. sudo R                                                                                                                    # RcppEigen was installed in the usr/local/lib/R/library, so sudo was needed
  12. install.packages(“TMB”, keep_outputs = TRUE)                                                    # saves log of installation in TMB.out file
The Matrix package was installed along with all the others when R was installed with no problem. The details of the above may be different in your case but the overall steps should be the same.

Hope this helps

Bob

messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Installation issue
parts:
Just to close this thread:
The problem installing TMB was Rcpp could not load libstdc++.so.6. Fixed
by installing libstdc++.so.6-dev.

Not strictly a TMB issue after all.

Thanks to Ben and Robert for their help.

John
